Here, the denominator is the imaginary number $5\text{i}.$ Note that this can be written as $0+5\text{i},$ so the conjugate is $0-5\text{i},$ or simply $-5\text{i}.$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-5\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5+2\text{i}}{5\text{i}} & =\frac{5+2\text{i}}{5\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-5\text{i}}{-5\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-25\text{i}-10{\text{i}}^{2}}{-25{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-25\text{i}-10(-1)}{-25(-1)} \\  & =\frac{10-25\text{i}}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{10-25\text{i}}{25} & =\frac{10}{25}-\frac{25}{25}\text{i} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}-\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
